facts.statement: Rafael Duarte scored from close range to make it 0-1 in the first minute.
The shot was taken from about six and a half metres at 87.6 km/h and went in.
The assist came from Chidi Balogun, a progressive ground pass that broke four lines.
Kingsport's chance swung the win probability massively: before the goal the away win chance was 38.71% and after it was 66.23%.
The moment moved the match's win probability by 27.5 percentage points (moment weight).
The decision model recorded Duarte's shot xG around 0.12 and the play-level xG was 0.1185; the model found no better passing alternative.

facts.statement: Kwame Mensah scored with an open-play right-foot finish to make it 1-1.
The goal was assisted by Yanis Besnard with a pressured ground cutback pass.
The shot’s model xG at the moment was 0.1103 and the options layer records the shot xG as 0.11.
The shot travelled about 13 metres and was struck at 89.2 km/h.
Riverside’s win probability rose from 0.082 before the goal to 0.3439 after it, a swing captured as a 26.2 moment weight.
Mensah now has one goal from four shots and 0.616 expected goals for the match so far.

brief.insight: Besnard’s pressured cutback created a clear, low-block lane and Mensah took a near-central, unpressured shot rather than forcing a riskier pass; the finish restored momentum and materially increased Riverside’s chances of winning. The play exposed Kingsport’s inability to close the space in the central channel immediately after the carry, letting Mensah get a clean strike.
brief.decision: Mensah chose to shoot from about 13 metres (choice xG 0.11). The stats layer found no better passing option (better_option_exists: false), so there was no available teammate with a higher completion×xG value than the shot; the shot choice was therefore the correct decision according to the model.

spec.question: What if Mensah had missed the 48th-minute shot?
spec.hypothesis: The shot (xG 0.1103) at 48' currently became a goal and swung Riverside from a very small pre-shot win probability (home 0.082, draw 0.2835, away 0.6346) to a much more balanced state after the goal (home 0.3439, draw 0.329, away 0.3271). If Mensah had missed instead, I expect the match to remain closer to the pre-shot state: Riverside would remain heavy underdogs and the most common simulated final result will be an away (opponent) win, with Riverside wins occurring only rarely (on the order of the low pre-shot win probability) and far fewer simulated comebacks than in the actual-game branch where the goal occurred.

brief.insight: Riverside elected for a power-driven direct attempt from distance into a narrow target area rather than probing a higher-value teammate. Kingsport’s keeper was already busy and positioned to react, so the low-xG but high-speed free kick still required a reflex save to prevent a dangerous shift in momentum.

brief.headline: Last-gasp penalty by Gilmartin wins it for Kingsport

facts.statement: Darragh Gilmartin scored a penalty to make it 2-1 for Kingsport in the 90+6 minute.
The penalty had an xG of 0.7385.
Before the kick, Riverside's win probability was 20.19%, the draw was 62.76% and Kingsport was 17.05%.
After the goal, Kingsport's win probability jumped to 90.31%, with Riverside at 0.75% and the draw at 8.94%.
The match swing from the penalty was a huge 73.3 percentage points of win probability.
The penalty was struck with a measured speed of 96.1 km/h from 11.0 metres.
The shooter chose to finish; the best available passing alternative on the stats layer was to Brennan with a 74% completion chance and an xG of 0.03 from his spot.

brief.insight: Kingsport took the straightforward, high-value option under no pressure: a penalty with an xG of 0.74. That single decision converted a likely draw into an almost certain win by removing Riverside's late comeback chance.
brief.decision: Gilmartin chose to shoot and scored. Best alternative on the stats layer was a pass to Brennan (74% pass completion, xG 0.03 from his spot). The shot was the right choice because the penalty xG of 0.7385 far exceeded the best teammate option's xG of 0.03.

spec.hypothesis: Because the penalty had xG 0.7385 and converting it changed the match win probability from (home 0.2019, draw 0.6276, away 0.1705) to (home 0.0075, draw 0.0894, away 0.9031), I expect that forcing this penalty to miss will reverse most of that swing: the away team should no longer be overwhelming favourites and many simulated futures will end in a draw (or a Riverside win) rather than an away win. In short, I expect far fewer away wins and many more draws/home results than the actual outcome, because a missed high-xG penalty late in stoppage would largely preserve the pre-penalty win/draw probabilities.
